text.en: Raju asked who is the head of his state. "The Governor and the Chief Minister," said his teacher.

Each state has a legislature, an executive and a judiciary. The Governor is the head of state, appointed by the President. The Chief Minister is the head of government and leads the Council of Ministers responsible to the Legislative Assembly.
The Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha) is directly elected and normally serves for five years unless dissolved sooner. Some states, like Tamil Nadu earlier, had a Legislative Council. State legislatures can make laws for State List subjects such as police and public health. They also share power over Concurrent List subjects under constitutional rules.
The High Court is the highest court of the state, and the Madras High Court serves Tamil Nadu. Local bodies and the state work together.
Each state has a legislature, an executive and a judiciary.

board.text: Legislative Assembly

text.en: Members of the Legislative Assembly are elected. Its normal term is five years from its first meeting, unless dissolved sooner.

text.en: Some states have a Legislative Council as well as a Legislative Assembly. Tamil Nadu formerly had a Council.

text.en: Local bodies and the state work together.

board.text: Chief Minister

text.en: State institutions exercise powers assigned by the Constitution. Their work can affect services such as public health, policing and education.

board.text: The Constitution assigns responsibilities

text.en: The President appoints a Governor. The Governor usually acts with the aid and advice of the state ministry, subject to the Constitution.

board.text: Governor: constitutional office

text.en: The Chief Minister leads the Council of Ministers. The other ministers are appointed by the Governor on the Chief Minister’s advice.

board.text: The Governor appoints the Chief Minister

text.en: The ministers are collectively responsible to the Assembly. The government normally needs the support of the elected House.

board.text: The Council is answerable to the Assembly

text.en: Voters in each Assembly constituency choose a representative. The abbreviation M L A stands for Member of the Legislative Assembly.

board.text: Constituencies elect MLAs

text.en: A state legislature consists of the Governor and one or two Houses. Every state has a Legislative Assembly.

board.text: The Governor is part of the legislature

text.en: In a state with a Legislative Council, there are two Houses. The Council continues while its members retire by rotation.

board.text: Some states also have a Council

text.en: Its elected House is the Legislative Assembly. Its former Legislative Council belongs to an earlier period.

board.text: Tamil Nadu has one legislative House

text.en: The Assembly chooses its Speaker from among its members. The Speaker conducts proceedings according to the House rules.

board.text: The Speaker presides over the Assembly

text.en: Public health is normally a State List subject. Education is on the Concurrent List, which gives lawmaking powers to both levels under constitutional rules.

board.text: State and Concurrent Lists have different roles

text.en: Members can debate a Bill and consider changes. The steps for passage depend on the type of Bill and the structure of the legislature.

board.text: A Bill is a proposal for a law

text.en: In a state with one House, a Bill passed by the Assembly is presented to the Governor. The Constitution provides for assent and other responses.

board.text: An Assembly-passed Bill goes to the Governor

text.en: A state Money Bill cannot be introduced in a Legislative Council. Where there is a Council, it can make recommendations to the Assembly.

board.text: State Money Bills originate in the Assembly

text.en: The annual financial statement gives estimated receipts and expenditure. The Assembly considers and votes on demands for grants.

board.text: The Assembly studies the use of public money

text.en: Members can ask ministers how a public programme is being carried out. Scrutiny gives representatives a way to ask for explanations.

board.text: Questions and debate scrutinise the executive

text.en: The Advocate General advises the state government on legal matters and carries out constitutional legal duties.

board.text: Advocate General: state legal advice

text.en: A High Court has jurisdiction according to the Constitution and laws. It can also supervise many courts and tribunals in its jurisdiction.

board.text: High Courts hear cases and appeals

text.en: Article Two Hundred and Twenty-Six gives High Courts powers to issue writs for Fundamental Rights and for other purposes.

board.text: High Courts can issue writs

text.en: The Constitution permits a common High Court for more than one state or for states and a Union territory.

board.text: One High Court can serve several territories

text.en: Its name reflects the historical name of the city of Chennai. The Constitution permits a High Court to have jurisdiction beyond one state.

board.text: Madras High Court serves Tamil Nadu

text.en: Panchayats and municipalities handle local responsibilities under state law. State departments can work with them on services such as water and sanitation.

board.text: Local bodies and state agencies can work together

text.en: An Assembly debates laws and scrutinises spending. Ministers administer public programmes. Courts decide disputes under law.

board.text: Tell the institutions apart by what they do

problem.en: What does the Chief Minister do?

text.en: Heads the state government.
Leads the Council of Ministers.
Is responsible to the Assembly.

problem.en: Who appoints the Chief Minister, and where must the ministry command confidence?

text.en: The Governor appoints the Chief Minister.
The Council is collectively responsible to the elected Assembly.

why.en: Government normally depends on the Assembly’s confidence.

problem.en: An MLA asks a minister about a state clinic programme. Which legislative role is this?

text.en: The MLA is seeking an explanation from the executive.

why.en: Ministers can be questioned about public administration.

text.en: This is legislative oversight.

why.en: It differs from deciding a court case.

problem.en: Why is Tamil Nadu described as having a one-House state legislature?

text.en: Tamil Nadu has an elected Legislative Assembly.

why.en: It is the one legislative House.

text.en: There is no sitting Legislative Council.

why.en: The Governor is still a constitutional part of the legislature.
